sanskrit_verse:
एवं वादिकृतान् वादान् प्रपश्येत् प्रत्यहं नृपः ।
नृपाश्रयास् तथा चान्ये विद्वद्भिर् ब्राह्मणैः सह ॥
transliteration: evaṁ vādikṛtān vādān prapaśyet pratyahaṁ nṛpaḥ | nṛpāśrayās tathā cānye vidvadbhir brāhmaṇaiḥ saha ||
sph_interpretive_translation: The King shall daily witness the disputes arising from litigants and observe those who take refuge in him, along with learned Brahmanas versed in Dharma.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority of the King as the living embodiment of Dharma
Causation rooted in conscious observation by the sovereign
Capacity-based responsibility through access to Dharma-knowers
Restoration logic via direct engagement with disputants
Consciousness alignment through daily exposure to dharmic resolution
executable_legal_axioms: IF a dispute arises THEN the King must observe it within one day
IF a subject takes royal refuge THEN their case shall be witnessed alongside learned Brahmanas
IF a dispute involves Dharma THEN it must be reviewed in presence of Vedic scholars
IF the King observes a dispute THEN no external punitive action shall proceed without his witnessing
supreme_court_application: At the highest judicial level, this verse establishes that ultimate adjudication requires sovereign-consciousness participation. The Supreme Court functions under the King's authority, ensuring that all legal matters are observed and resolved in alignment with Sanatana Dharma through learned Brahmanas.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa is established through the King's direct perception and the testimony of Vedic knowers. Anupūrvaśaḥ ensures sequential manifestation of truth when both temporal and scriptural authorities align. Responsibility lies in correct observation, not infliction. Truth emerges through conscious witnessing, not coercion.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Daily hearing protocol for all disputes brought before the sovereign
Mandatory inclusion of learned Brahmanas in complex dharmic cases
Refugee-integration process where subjects are assured audience and guidance
Completion mechanism wherein unresolved matters remain open until properly witnessed
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as the Source of Law. Dharma is restored through conscious observation and dharmic authority. Reality remains non-punitive, guided solely by the sovereign's alignment with Sanatana Truth. Consciousness stands as the ultimate adjudicator.
